messages:
anna: quick sync re: continuous-batcher degradation strategy. refactor will change some invariants, we need a clear, testable contract for transitions so downstream teams are not surprised

diego: agreed. sketching constraints: (1) deterministic transition graph, (2) per-tenant decision cache with TTL, (3) bounded evaluation cost on enqueue path

li: i want a readable policy shape that ops can inspect. propose a small JSON-ish policy with explicit priority order. example: {"modes":["coalesce","microfall","quant","shed"],"edges":[{"from":"coalesce","to":"microfall","cond":"p99>40ms && kv_miss>0.15"}]}

anna: good. prefer human-friendly YAML in repo, but runtime can ingest a compiled JSON. also include metadata on edges: min_stay_ms, hysteresis_factor, severity_tag

ophelia: ops requirements: - ability to annotate a tenant with "sticky-mode" for debugging - auto-recovery window so forced modes expire - human-readable audit entries for each transition

sre-bot: alert: last 15m saw 3 nodes hit kv_cache_miss>0.2; two tenants observed oscillation of mode changes > 6 times in 60s

diego: about oscillation: we need two levers: (A) global min_dwell_ms and (B) per-tenant damping that increases TTL on repeated transitions. damping could be linear or multiplicative

li: implementation idea: represent each tenant decision as {mode, expiry_ts, reason_hash, flip_count}. flip_count increments when reason_hash changes; use it to inflate expiry

anna: what about signals? enumerating common signals: p50/p95/p99 latency, kv_cache_miss_ratio, input_tokens_per_sec, backend_queue_depth, node_memory_pressure

ophelia: add: active_gpu_fraction and io_wait_ms. both matter for degradation decisions on Dedicated machines

li: telemetry plan: emit a labeled event on transition: metric name `scheduler.mode_transition` with tags tenant, from, to, reason, flip_count. also expose a trace span when edge evaluation runs with tag `edge:NAME`

diego: billing/visibility: include an enum for mode_impact {NONE, LATENCY_DEG, QUALITY_DEG, REJECT}. we can later use this to show teams a dashboard (why costs changed)

anna: question on placement: should evaluation run synchronously in enqueue path? concern: any blocking work there increases enqueue latency and can ripple to clients

li: plan: synchronous fetch of cached decision (fast), async refresh on background tick. but also allow synchronous fast-eval for a small set of signals that are constant-time (e.g., cached node-level counters). heavy checks only on tick

ophelia: also need a forced fallback trigger: if node-level headroom drops below threshold, then global-mode switch (node-wide) happens and per-tenant decisions are short-circuited to a degraded node-mode until headroom recovers

sre-bot: note: global-mode changes should be rare and require logging to postmortem channel when triggered more than once per hour

li: config sketch (YAML):

modes:
  - id: coalesce
    semantics: "primary, low-latency, full-quality"
  - id: microfall
    semantics: "short-window microqueue fallback"
  - id: quant
    semantics: "lower-precision lanes"
  - id: shed
    semantics: "soft-reject or rate-limit"
edges:
  - from: coalesce
    to: microfall
    cond: "p99 > 40ms || kv_miss > 0.18"
    min_stay_ms: 500
    hysteresis: 1.5

  - from: microfall
    to: quant
    cond: "node_headroom < 0.12 && backend_queue > 50"
    min_stay_ms: 1000
    severity: QUALITY_DEG

  - from: quant
    to: shed
    cond: "sustained_load > 0.9"
    min_stay_ms: 2000
    severity: REJECT

anna: that covers most cases. a couple of tradeoffs to call out: (1) complexity vs control: more modes = finer-grained recovery but harder to test. (2) telemetry volume if we emit every tiny flip.

diego: testing matrix: unit tests for graph correctness, property tests for no immediate cycles, long-run simulation with shuffled multi-tenant traces, canary rollout on a small fleet with forced-mode injection, and a rollback plan if coalesce latency regresses > 10%

li: migration: default policy should replicate current heuristics. policy under feature flag initially. rollout phases: lab -> canary (5% traffic) -> staggered 25% steps -> global


ophelia: UX: return header `X-Redwood-Mode: quant` and a small debug JSON in response when `?redwood_debug=1` so app teams can adapt behavior. RBAC required for debug toggles

anna: ops integration: provide a console view with per-tenant recent mode timeline and a histogram of durations. useful for support triage

sre-bot: build: admission-adapter v0.1.1 pushed. e2e test scheduled on canary cluster at 02:00 UTC tomorrow

diego: action items: li -> put policy schema in repo + example sets; anna -> RFC followup with invariants & migration plan; ophelia -> console mockups and RBAC notes; i'll own simulation harness and run initial fuzzing

li: one more micro-optimization: represent condition predicates as compiled lambda IDs (no parsing on hot path). the build step compiles YAML into a tiny bytecode the runtime interprets cheaply

anna: love it. small follow-ups: add a throttling escape hatch that converts soft-shed into hard-reject after X minutes of continuous rehases for a tenant. prevents runaway cost

ophelia: noted. we'll also add an SLO-based automated revert: if global p99 increases more than threshold after rollout, revert policy in 5m window automatically

li: thanks all. i'll open the PR for policy schema and a converter. linking it to admission-adapter build.

anna: thanks team. short and actionable. :white_check_mark:
